senses.definition: To record the departure or withdrawal of someone or something (such as guests, employees, books, etc.).
senses.example: He checked his favorite mystery out for the twenty-third time.

senses.definition: To record one's departure from a workplace, hotel, restaurant, etc.
senses.example: Be sure to check out of the hotel before noon.

senses.definition: To examine, inspect, look at closely, ogle; to investigate; to gather information so as to make a decision.
senses.example: He was hanging out at the beach, checking out the young women in bikinis.

senses.definition: To obtain source code (or other material) from a source control repository so that one can modify it (and often later check in the modified version).
To become uninterested in an activity and cease to participate in more than a perfunctory manner; to become uncooperative.
senses.example: The purpose of this exercise was to ignite reactions from students, but over the few years I used it, it backfired, culminating in a situation where I lost a significant number of the white students, who just "checked out" for the rest of the semester.

senses.definition: To become catatonic or otherwise nonresponsive.
senses.example: Even during those years, there would be a lot of times she just checked out. She would be sitting there looking at her nails and she'd just be gone.

Steve: (referring to his girlfriend attempting suicide in front of both of them) Look, I was just an observer.
Bishop: You haven't answered my question.
Steve: Well, what do you think?
Bishop: We'll never know, will we?
Steve: Well, say I just sat there—or we just sat there—and watched her check out. Think that would have been crazy?

senses.definition: To prove (after an investigation) to be the case, or to be in order.
senses.example: The first two leads check out; I'll assume the third one is also valid.

senses.definition: To visit the oche for the last time and clear one's remaining points to win the game.
